ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording a total wind output of 12.1 GW, with Scottish wind generation contributing an estimated 1.0 GW, which corresponds to 9.9% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Local renewable production keeps Scottish carbon intensity at an optimal 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in sharp contrast to the GB-wide average of 61 gCO2/kWh. Transmission network limitations, however, continue to force clean power offline. Scottish generation curtailed so far today stands at 204 MWh through Balancing Mechanism actions, accumulating a constraint cost of about £6,641. To replace this rejected Scottish wind output, thermal plants were dispatched across other regions, resulting in an estimated 38,741 cubic meters of gas burned elsewhere and emitting 71 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualizing this single-day figure across 365 days indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £2 million rounded to the nearest million. While these recurring constraint payments ultimately feed into system balancing charges paid by consumers, deriving the exact £/MWh increase applied to consumer invoices across the UK cannot be calculated without relying on total national electricity demand figures that lie outside the authorized dataset.
